input.strategy_title: Experiment comparison for training and pipeline runs
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Data scientists iterate across dozens of training and pipeline runs but have no
way to compare them inside the platform: parameters and metrics live in
per-run pages, so comparison happens in exported spreadsheets. Model promotion
decisions need side-by-side visibility into what changed between candidate
runs and how their metrics differ. (Requirements below were consolidated from
two customer councils; some overlap in wording was kept from the sources.)

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Registered model versions link back to the run that produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Provide a run "diff" view that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs list and the registry. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Model Registry
- Data Science Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automatic best-run selection or promotion
- Comparison across clusters or across projects

## Open Questions

None.

# Side-by-side and diff comparison of run parameters and metrics in the Dashboard

## Description

This epic delivers the run comparison capability in the Dashboard: users can select two or more training and pipeline runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side, and switch to a diff view that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs. This replaces the current export-to-spreadsheet workflow for comparing candidate runs during model promotion decisions.

## Scope

- Multi-select of runs from the runs list (covering both training and pipeline runs).
- Side-by-side view of parameters and metrics for the selected runs.
- Diff view over two selected runs that highlights which parameters and metrics changed; the diff view is a presentation mode of the same comparison surface, delivered together with the side-by-side view.
- The comparison reads the per-run parameter and metric data the Dashboard already surfaces on per-run pages; the Dashboard owns no data plane, so no new backend data store is introduced.
- Validation against Data Science Pipelines run data (passive component — no Data Science Pipelines code changes are expected): the comparison is exercised against real pipeline runs through the existing run-data surfaces.
- Out of scope: automatic best-run selection or promotion, and comparison across clusters or projects.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given two or more runs selected from the runs list, When the user opens the comparison, Then the parameters and metrics of all selected runs are displayed side by side.
- Given exactly two runs selected in the comparison, When the user switches to the diff view, Then every parameter and metric key present in either run is shown with changed values highlighted — measured by: the diff lists the union of keys from both runs and marks each key whose value differs.
- Given runs of both kinds, When compared, Then the comparison works for training runs and for pipeline runs — measured by: a side-by-side and a diff comparison succeeds against real pipeline runs retrieved through the existing run-data surfaces, with no Data Science Pipelines code change required.
- Given the comparison is open, When the user changes the run selection, Then the side-by-side and diff views update accordingly.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)** — Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard: fully covered by this epic.
- **HLR-3 (P1)** — Provide a run "diff" view that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs: covered by this epic, **bundled** with HLR-1. The diff view is a presentation mode of the same comparison surface over the same run data (same component, same team, same UI surface); it edits the same call sites and data structures as the side-by-side view, so splitting it out would double-touch the same surface and is not separately schedulable. The epic is prioritized at the higher of the two levels (P0).

# Run linkage on registered model versions in the Model Registry

## Description

This epic delivers the data side of run lineage in the Model Registry: registered model versions record a link back to the run that produced them, using the Model Registry's extension point for structured metadata on model versions, so that downstream consumers (such as the Dashboard) can resolve the originating run of any registered version.

## Scope

- Define and implement the run-linkage representation on registered model versions, so each version carries a reference to the run that produced it.
- Support populating the linkage at registration time, so registering clients (e.g. a pipeline step or user registering a model) can record the originating run.
- Make the linkage readable through the Model Registry REST API entity model, so the Dashboard and other consumers can retrieve the originating run for a given model version.
- The specific property/field naming and population mechanism are implementation decisions for the Model Registry team; the epic's scope is the capability, not a specific schema.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a model version registered from a run, When the version is retrieved through the Model Registry REST API, Then the response includes a reference to the run that produced it.
- Given a set of registered model versions, When queried via the API, Then the run linkage is retrievable for every version registered with lineage — measured by: an API query returns the originating-run reference for each such version.
- Given a model version registered without a known originating run, When retrieved, Then the linkage is absent or empty without breaking the entity (the link is optional metadata, not a required field).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P1)** — Registered model versions link back to the run that produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry: this epic covers the data half (the linkage recorded on model versions and exposed via the registry API). The UI half (opening a comparison from the registry) is delivered by the Dashboard registry-integration epic.

# Open run comparison from the Model Registry (Dashboard registry integration)

## Description

This epic delivers the registry-side entry point for run comparison in the Dashboard: from a registered model version's view in the Model Registry UI, users can see the run that produced the version and open a run comparison populated with that run, reusing the run comparison capability already delivered for the runs list.

## Scope

- In the Dashboard's Model Registry model-version view, surface the originating-run linkage recorded on the model version.
- Provide an action that opens the run comparison (the side-by-side and diff capability delivered for the runs list) with the linked run pre-selected, alongside the ability to add further runs to the comparison.
- No new comparison surface is built in this epic — the registry entry point populates and navigates to the existing comparison views.
- Works for both the side-by-side mode and the diff mode of the comparison.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a registered model version that carries a run linkage, When the user views the version in the Model Registry UI, Then the originating run is shown.
- Given a registered model version that carries a run linkage, When the user opens the comparison from the registry, Then the comparison view opens with the linked run pre-selected and further runs selectable — measured by: the opened comparison displays the linked run's parameters and metrics alongside at least one other run.
- Given the comparison opened from the registry, When the user switches to the diff view with a second run selected, Then changed parameters and metrics are highlighted.
- Given a model version with no run linkage, When viewed in the registry UI, Then the comparison entry point is absent or disabled without breaking the version view.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P1)** — Registered model versions link back to the run that produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry: this epic covers the UI half (the registry-side entry point that opens a comparison). The data half (the linkage recorded on model versions) is delivered by the Model Registry epic.

# Documentation for the run comparison workflow

## Description

This epic delivers user documentation for the run comparison workflow: how to select runs and compare their parameters and metrics side by side, how to use the diff view, and how to open a comparison from a registered model version in the Model Registry.

## Scope

Content outline:

- New documentation topics covering the end-to-end comparison workflow:
  - Selecting two or more training or pipeline runs from the runs list and viewing their parameters and metrics side by side.
  - Using the diff view to see which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs.
  - Opening a comparison from the Model Registry, starting from a registered model version's run linkage.
- Coverage of both entry points: the runs list and the Model Registry.
- Procedures and screenshots matching the shipped UI.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the published documentation, When a reader follows the comparison procedure from the runs list, Then the steps match the shipped UI and lead to a working side-by-side comparison.
- Given the published documentation, When a reader follows the procedure for opening a comparison from the Model Registry, Then the steps match the shipped UI and lead to a working comparison opened from a registered model version.
- The diff-view topic documents how changed parameters and metrics are highlighted.
- Documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented comparison and registry-linkage behavior — measured by: a review by the implementing engineers confirms accuracy, recorded before publication.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)** — Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs list and the registry: fully covered by this epic.
